headline: Last session: Sensex fell 289 points and Nifty slipped on inflation concerns, though markets extended weekly gains.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 17 November.

why: Inflation concerns weighed on investor sentiment during the last trading session.
Foreign institutional investor (FII) buying backed the broader market momentum over the week.
Expectations of lower crude oil prices supported early trade gains prior to Friday's decline.
Global AI stock retreat fueled a rotation trade benefiting Indian equities.
whatHappening: In the last session, Sensex dropped 289 points as Nifty also closed lower due to inflation worries.
Sensex and Nifty registered gains for the third straight week, with smallcaps rising 3.6% and PSU banks surging 7.5%.
Upcoming market cues include WPI inflation data, crude oil prices, and FII trading activity.
House of Abhinandan Lodha prepaid a ₹1,100 crore loan to HDFC Capital.
summary:
In the last trading session, Indian benchmark indices closed lower as Sensex fell 289 points amid inflation concerns.
Despite Friday's decline, Sensex and Nifty extended gains for the third consecutive week supported by sustained FII inflows.
Market focus moving forward will remain on upcoming WPI inflation data, global crude oil prices, and foreign investor trends.
